A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all six articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the first article of six.

Introduction

My wife and I had the privilege of having a courtship without regrets or guilt. We were blessed with parents who guided us in the right way and gave us opportunities that they didn’t have.

If you don’t have that testimony or memory, please don’t go on a guilt trip. But my prayer for you is that you get a burning burden and vision in your heart to have it for your children. That can be your reward.

A Christ-centered courtship is a period of time between a single life and a married life. The decisions you make in this period will affect you for the rest of your lives. With God’s blessing on your life, you can end up with no regrets or guilt.

Five goals for this Christ-Centered Courtship series.

Goal #1. To turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.

Goal #2. To turn the hearts of the children to their fathers.

Goal #3. That parents would get a burden to lead each one of their children into the perfect will of God for their lives.

Goal #4. That young people would get a burden to seek after God, find fulfillment and purpose in walking with God, and you would seek maturity in your manners and in your character.

Goal #5. That young men and young women would rise up to be godly fathers and godly mothers with a vision to raise up another godly generation, and the Gospel of Jesus Christ can go on.

God’s Plan for Male and Female

Ecclesiastes 12:1 says, “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.” My desire is that each one of you, remember your Creator in the days of your youth. Turn your heart, your focus, and your life to pursue after your Creator, Almighty God, in heaven.

What does he mean, “while the evil days come not” and “the years draw nigh”? It means to seek the Lord when you’re young. Take the energy of your youth and seek after God. Young people, you’re young and full of ideas, visions, plans, and dreams. I doubt there are any of you who just enjoy sitting down in an easy chair, putting your feet up, and just dreaming about how terrible and horrible life is going to be. We don’t do that, do we? But if we don’t walk with God and follow God’s plan, hard things will come upon us. When hard things come in life, we have no place to turn to. We dream that life will turn out well. The decisions and actions in our youth affect us for the rest of our lives. The good news is they can affect us in a good way. The bad news is they can affect us in a bad way. It depends on what decisions and choices we make. But young people, you’re young, and you have the opportunity to choose.

Let’s go to the beginning of Genesis.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Genesis 2:18). “I’ll make him an help that is meet for him.” God said He would do that.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). God made. God created us male and female. It takes a lot of blind faith to believe that we evolved perfectly as male and female. The creation of male and female is God’s plan. It is one of the living proofs of Creation. God made. God created. It’s God’s plan. God is the Author. And God’s plan brings blessing.

I’d like to look at ten different aspects of this blessing of God’s plan.

1) God brings Eve to Adam.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (Genesis 2:22-23).

God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. Then God created Eve and brought her to Adam. Adam awoke and realized, “This one is for me!” He had seen all the animals go by when he named them. Now God brings him someone that is for him. He also realized, “She was taken out of my side.” She’s close to his heart. “This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.” It’s not a dog; it’s not a giraffe, or a monkey, or an ape. This one that God brought to him is like him. God’s plan has a blessing.

Adam and Eve had never had a companion before. Adam and Eve had never let the emotions of their heart go before. Something happened in Adam and Eve’s hearts. Adam was a “one-woman man,” and Eve was a “one-man woman.” They never gave their heart passions to anybody else. God has that plan for us, too. God’s plan brings blessings.

2) Leaving and cleaving in unity for life.

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

This verse says, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother,” but Adam and Eve did not have a father and mother. What God is saying it doesn’t work for there to be cleaving unless there’s leaving. Also, in Mark 10:7, we read, “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.” This is God’s plan, and God’s plan brings blessing.

Leaving means to leave behind, to abandon. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother” is to leave parents leave behind. Let’s consider a young man who has a really good home life. He’s blessed and has everything he needs. Yet once God brings his Eve into his life, something rises up inside him, and he says, “I’m leaving!” But this is God’s plan. And God’s plan brings blessing.

It’s not just leaving his father and mother; he also cleaves to his wife. Cleave means “to glue to, to adhere.” We are very familiar with glued wood panels. All kinds of solid furniture are made out of panels glued together. And if they’re glued together right, they will not come apart at the joints. If you tear them apart, you’re going to have to tear the wood apart. God’s glue is the same way, where it glues two people together. The only way to tear them apart is by splintering and ripping and God does not bless that. But leaving and cleaving, staying together and being glued together, that’s God’s plan and it brings blessing.

3) They shall be one flesh.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Two single people who become one married couple, become one unit before God, and become one family before God. They become one flesh, where God sees them as together as one.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Mark 10:8-9). God’s plan for male and female is that He brings Eve to Adam. Then the leaving and cleaving to take place. He causes them to become one flesh. Pulling apart is no blessing at all but bringsagony,pain,travail, and hurt. There is no blessing in separation. But God’s plan brings blessing.

4) Not an unequal yoke.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Corinthians 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:39).

God’s plan is that marriage is an equal yoke. God will not bring an Eve to an Adam in a marriage that is an unequal yoke.Let’s think about leaving and cleaving, getting glued together, and two becoming one. In marriage, those two are now one before God. Imagine being in a bad marriage relationship like this—a family like this trying to function together. There will be no blessing.

But an equal yoke brings blessing! God desires that we be joined together in one flesh, one heart, and one mind. He wants to see us joined in heart, mind, and fleashthe whole being, being one. God’s plan brings blessing.

5) God planned for us to have children.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:28). Think of the joy and miracle every time another child is born into a Christian home. God planned it this way. And if God brought Adam his Eve, and they leave and cleave, they become one flesh, one heart, one mind. If they are equally yoked and God blesses them with children, it becomes a joyful haven where God can dwell. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (Genesis 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (Genesis 9:7). God’s plan brings blessing.

6) Headship order.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Corinthians 11:3). It is God, and then Christ, the man, and the woman. God established a headship order, and this headship order is a blessing. It’s God’s plan, and it’s a blessing.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Ephesians 6:1-3). . Children, obey your parents in the Lord is a part of the headship order. This not difficult to understand, is it? A home following the plan of God is just a blessed situation. Young people learn to be under authority. Make that your high priority. The sooner you learn to be under authority, the better you will be prepared for the responsibilities in life.

I remember looking at married life and having aspirations about teaching children and raising a godly family. I listened to the “Godly Home” series and thought I was ready to go. But then the day came when it was my turn and my responsibility, and all of a sudden, my heart wanted to wither. Responsibility doesn’t feel the same as dreaming about it does. YOU need to do something! YOU are responsible. YOU need to make it happen. And, by the way, not just make it happen; you need to make it happen in a Christlike way. You need to make it happen in a way that the anointing of the Spirit of God can come down on your family. The better we learn how to be under authority, the better we’ll be prepared for those responsibilities. The more we realize we need God, the better off we are. Let’s make a high priority out of learning to be under authority as children and as young people. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Proverbs 3:1-2).

God will add his blessing if we stay in this headship order. The more you learn how to be under authority, the more you will be blessed when you establish your home. God’s plan has blessings.

7) A godly marriage.

Ephesians 5:21,22,24 says, “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”

First of all look at verse 21, “submitting yourselves one to another.” There’s a blending together that needs to happen in a godly home. This blending together should happen in the fear of God. If we’re submitting one to another in the fear of God, we’re going to obey God because we want His blessings.

Ephesians 5: 22, 24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Young ladies, you can count on it: submission to Dad equals submission to a husband. You can practice while you are single. This will help build character in your life. Being a rebellious and froward woman is not going to bring the blessing of God.

It goes on and says, in Ephesians 5:25,28,29. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” Young men, this says that husbands should love their wives. So who do you think God put in your life to prepare you to love your wife? Your mother! Do you want to learn how to love your wife? Learn how to get along with your mom, love your mom, and care about her. Do you want to practice to love your future wife? Go ahead and love your mom.

Verse 33, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” God’s plan brings blessings.

8) Being heirs together of the grace of life.

1 Peter 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” As husbands, we give honor to the wife. She is the weaker vessel and the one that born the children! She’s gone through a lot of traumatic changes in her life. She’s the one that gets worn out and tires sooner.

And he says, “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

Young men, learn to understand your mom and your sisters. It will help you after you get married. Don’t conclude that—ah, that’s just women. No, you want the blessing of God. Learn to know and understand them.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” God wants us to be heirs together of the grace of life. If we’re not heirs together of the grace of life, can we be heirs separated of the grace of life? I don’t think so. He says we should be heirs together so that our prayers are not hindered. So if we’re heirs separated, could we say our prayers will be hindered? Yes, our prayers will be hindered. Let’s give honor unto the wife as unto the weaker vessel. Every ounce you can gain in this area will only bless you later. It’s worth it. God’s plan brings blessing.

9) A blessed and secure home.

This comes partly out of 1 Peter 3:7, but also from Psalm 144:12 “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” The grace of God is on a secure home where there is unity. Where Dad is understanding Mom, where Dad cares about Mom. Dad is ministering and is there to help and guide. He’s there to give direction with a heart of compassion. God’s plan for male and female—God’s plan brings blessings.

10) As Christ and the church.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church” (Ephesians 5:24-29).

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave Himself for it.” God is looking for men who are willing to give their lives. Single young men, who are willing to answer the call and give their life. This is a high calling of God. It’s the plan of God.

Young men, are you willing to lay down your life, your agenda, and those independent things you like to do? Are you willing to be patient, gentle, and understanding? Are you willing to lose sleep and keep going even when you’re tired? Are you willing to stay calm and not react in stressful circumstances? Are you willing to lead and guide a wife and children, eternal souls, through this life?

But my plea is that you would volunteer and say, “I’m willing to apply myself to the Word of God, the will of God, the plan of God, and I’ll give my life. I’m willing to lay it on the altar.” Jesus gave His life for us, and He’s comparing the marriage with the church and Him.

There’s also a need for mothers who are submissive and yielded to authority. Mothers who do not follow the women’s lib of our day but are rather content to be keepers at home.

Young ladies, are you willing to enlist? Will you give your heart to be guided and led? Are you willing to follow and to cheerfully submit to your authority? Are you willing to serve and be spent for your family? Are you willing to serve and be spent for YOUR family? If you get married someday, it will be YOUR family that you’ll be serving and being spent for. Are you willing to bear pain and discomfort? Are you willing to be a helpmeet, giving yourself for his burden and vision?

But as we look at God’s plan and blessings, you want God’s blessing, young people! But that means you need to make choices accordingly. Rise up and make decisions that will lead to maturity. Maturity comes with the process of seeking after God. Make a commitment in your heart to open yourself to God’s blessings and principles. I encourage you to walk with God, to have a relationship with Jesus Christ, and to do so in humility.

Seek after Christlike character, and do it on purpose. It is so easy for us to just live life however it happens. But if we make decisions on purpose, it will take us somewhere! Those decisions matter. Do things according to God’s plan.

God has a plan for male and female and he has a plan for you.

그리스도를 중심으로 한 구혼(A Christ-centered Courtship)은 폴 허시버거(Paul Hershberger)가 설교한 경건한 구혼에 관한 일련의 설교입니다. 지난 십 년 동안 여러 장소에서 여러 차례 이 설교를 전했습니다. 최근 우리는 이를 필기록으로 옮기고 가독성을 위해 요약했습니다. 모든 여섯 편의 기사를 The Heartbeat of the Remnant에 게재한 후 소책자로 출간할 예정입니다. 이것은 여섯 편 중 첫 번째 기사입니다.

소개

제 아내와 저는 후회나 죄책감 없는 구혼의 특권을 누렸습니다. 저희는 자녀들을 올바른 길로 인도하고 자신들이 갖지 못했던 기회를 내어주신 부모님들로 말미암아 복을 받았습니다.

그 같은 증언이나 기억이 없다 해도 죄책감에 빠지지 마십시오. 그러나 저의 기도는 여러분이 자녀들을 위해 그런 것을 갖고자 하는 뜨거운 부담과 비전을 마음에 갖게 되시라는 것입니다. 그것이 여러분의 상이 될 수 있습니다.

그리스도를 중심으로 한 구혼은 독신의 삶과 결혼의 삶 사이의 기간입니다. 이 기간에 내리는 결정들은 여러분의 남은 생애에 영향을 미칩니다. 하나님께서 여러분의 삶에 복을 주신다면 후회나 죄책감 없이 마칠 수 있습니다.

이 그리스도 중심의 구혼 연재의 다섯 가지 목표

목표 #1. 아버지들의 마음이 자녀들에게로 향하게 하는 것.

목표 #2. 자녀들의 마음이 아버지들에게로 향하게 하는 것.

목표 #3. 부모들이 각 자녀를 하나님의 그분의 완전한 뜻으로 인도하려는 부담을 갖게 하는 것.

목표 #4. 젊은이들이 하나님을 찾는 부담을 갖고, 하나님과 동행함에서 충만함과 목적을 찾으며, 예절과 인격의 성숙을 추구하게 하는 것.

목표 #5. 젊은 남녀들이 경건한 아버지와 경건한 어머니로 일어서서 또 다른 경건한 세대를 일으키려는 비전을 품게 하여 예수 그리스도의 복음이 계속 전파되게 하는 것.

남성과 여성에 대한 하나님의 계획

전도서 12:1은 “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.”라고 말합니다. 저의 소망은 여러분 각자가 젊음의 날들에 너희의 창조주를 기억하는 것입니다. 마음과 초점을 돌려 하늘에 계신 전능하신 하나님, 너희의 창조주를 좇으십시오.

“while the evil days come not”와 “the years draw nigh”가 무슨 뜻입니까? 그것은 젊을 때 주님을 찾으라는 뜻입니다. 젊음의 기운을 가져다가 하나님을 찾아라. 젊은이들이여, 여러분은 젊고 생각, 비전, 계획과 꿈으로 가득합니다. 편한 의자에 앉아 발을 올려놓고 인생이 얼마나 끔찍하고 끔찍할지 꿈꾸는 것을 즐기는 사람이 있겠느냐고 저는 의심합니다. 우리는 그렇게 하지 않지요? 그러나 우리가 하나님과 동행하지 않고 하나님의 계획을 따르지 않으면 어려운 일이 닥칩니다. 인생에 어려움이 닥칠 때 우리는 기댈 데가 없습니다. 우리는 인생이 잘되기를 꿈꿉니다. 젊은 시절의 결정과 행동은 남은 생애에 영향을 미칩니다. 좋은 소식은 그것이 좋은 쪽으로 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 것입니다. 나쁜 소식은 나쁜 쪽으로 영향을 미칠 수도 있다는 것입니다. 그것은 우리가 어떤 결정과 선택을 하느냐에 달려 있습니다. 그러나 젊은이들이여, 여러분은 젊고 선택할 기회를 가지고 있습니다.

창세기의 시작으로 가봅시다.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Genesis 2:18). “I’ll make him an help that is meet for him.” 하나님은 그렇게 하시겠다고 말씀하셨습니다.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). 하나님이 만드셨습니다. 하나님이 우리를 남자와 여자로 창조하셨습니다. 우리가 남성과 여성으로 완벽하게 진화했다고 믿으려면 많은 맹목적 믿음이 필요합니다. 남성과 여성의 창조는 하나님의 계획입니다. 그것은 창조의 살아 있는 증거 중 하나입니다. 하나님이 만드셨습니다. 하나님이 창조하셨습니다. 이것은 하나님의 계획입니다. 하나님이 저자이십니다. 그리고 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

이 복의 측면을 열 가지로 살펴보겠습니다.

1) 하나님은 이브를 아담에게로 데려오신다.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (Genesis 2:22-23).

하나님은 아담을 깊은 잠에 들게 하셨습니다. 그다음 하나님은 이브를 창조하여 아담에게로 데려오셨습니다. 아담이 깨어나서 깨달았습니다. “이 사람은 내 것을 위한 사람이다!” 그는 모든 동물들이 지나가며 이름 붙이는 것을 보았습니다. 이제 하나님은 그에게 그의 것을 데려오셨습니다. 그는 또한 깨달았습니다. “그녀는 내 곁에서 취해졌다.” 그녀는 그의 마음 가까이에 있습니다. “This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.” 개도 아니고 기린도 아니며 원숭이나 유인원도 아닙니다. 하나님이 그에게 데려오신 이 사람은 그와 닮았습니다. 하나님의 계획에는 복이 있습니다.

아담과 이브는 이전에 동반자를 가져본 적이 없었습니다. 아담과 이브는 이전에 마음의 감정을 다른 데로 보낸 적도 없었습니다. 아담과 이브의 마음속에 무언가 일어났습니다. 아담은 “한 여자에게 충실한 남자”였고, 이브는 “한 남자에게 충실한 여자”였습니다. 그들은 마음의 정열을 다른 누구에게도 주지 않았습니다. 하나님께서 우리를 위해서도 그런 계획을 가지셨습니다. 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

2) 평생을 위한 떠남과 굳게 붙음(leave and cleave).

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

이 구절은 “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother”라 말하지만, 아담과 이브에게는 아버지와 어머니가 없었습니다. 하나님이 말씀하시는 것은 떠남이 없이는 굳게 붙음이 제대로 작동하지 않는다는 것입니다. 또한 마가복음 10:7에서 우리는 “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.”를 읽습니다. 이것은 하나님의 계획이며 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

떠난다는 것은 뒤에 남기고 떠나라는 뜻입니다. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother”는 부모를 뒤에 두고 떠나는 것을 의미합니다. 정말 좋은 가정에서 자란 젊은이를 생각해 봅시다. 그는 복을 받아 필요한 모든 것을 갖추고 있습니다. 그러나 하나님이 그의 이브를 그의 삶에 데려오시면, 그의 안에서 무언가가 일어나 “나는 떠난다!”라고 하게 됩니다. 그러나 이것이 하나님의 계획입니다. 그리고 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

그가 그의 아버지와 어머니만 떠나는 것이 아닙니다; 그는 또한 그의 아내에게 굳게 붙습니다. cleave는 “접착되다, 들러붙다”는 뜻입니다. 우리는 접착한 목재 판에 매우 익숙합니다. 모든 종류의 견고한 가구는 접착된 판으로 만들어집니다. 제대로 접착되면 이음새에서 떨어지지 않습니다. 그것을 찢으려면 목재 자체를 갈라야 합니다. 하나님의 접착력도 이와 같아서 두 사람을 단단히 붙입니다. 그것을 갈라놓는 유일한 방법은 쪼개고 찢어 버리는 것인데 하나님은 그것을 복되게 여기지 않습니다. 그러나 떠나고 굳게 붙어 함께 있고 접착되는 것, 그것이 하나님의 계획이며 복을 가져옵니다.

3) 그들이 한 몸이 된다.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). 두 명의 독신이 결혼하여 한 부부가 되면 하나님 앞에서 하나의 단위가 되고 하나님 앞에서 한 가정이 됩니다. 그들은 한 몸이 되어 하나님께서 그들을 함께 하나로 보십니다.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Mark 10:8-9). 하나님이 남자와 여자를 위하여 계획하신 것은 그가 이브를 아담에게 데려오시고, 떠나고 굳게 붙음이 일어나게 하시며, 그들이 한 몸이 되게 하시는 것입니다. 갈라놓는 것은 전혀 복이 아니며 오히려 고통과 근심과 산통과 상처를 가져옵니다. 분리는 복이 아닙니다. 그러나 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

4) 불평등한 멍에가 아니다.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Corinthians 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:39).

하나님의 계획은 결혼이 동등한 멍에라는 것입니다. 하나님은 불평등한 멍에인 결혼에서 이브를 아담에게 데려오지 않으십니다. 떠나고 굳게 붙고 함께 접착되어 둘이 한 몸이 되는 것을 생각해 보십시오. 결혼에서는 그 둘이 이제 하나님 앞에서 하나입니다. 이런 나쁜 관계의 결혼을 상상해 보십시오—그런 가정이 함께 기능하려 한다면 복이 없습니다.

그러나 동등한 멍에는 복을 가져옵니다! 하나님은 우리가 한 몸, 한 마음, 한 생각으로 연합하기를 원하십니다. 그는 우리가 마음과 생각과 살 전체로 연합해 있기를 보기를 원하십니다. 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

5) 하나님은 우리에게 자녀를 주도록 계획하셨다.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:28). 경건한 가정에 또 다른 자녀가 태어날 때마다 느끼는 기쁨과 기적을 생각해 보십시오. 하나님은 이렇게 계획하셨습니다. 만일 하나님이 아담에게 그의 이브를 데려오시고 그들이 떠나고 굳게 붙어 한 몸, 한 마음, 한 생각이 되며, 동등한 멍에를 지고 하나님이 자녀로 축복하신다면 그것은 하나님이 거하실 수 있는 기쁨의 안식처가 됩니다. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (Genesis 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (Genesis 9:7). 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

6) 머리의 질서(headship order).

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Corinthians 11:3). 하나님이 계시고, 그 다음에 그리스도, 남자, 여자입니다. 하나님은 머리의 질서를 세우셨고 이 머리의 질서는 복입니다. 하나님의 계획이며 복입니다.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Ephesians 6:1-3). 자녀들아, 주 안에서 부모에게 순종하라는 것은 머리의 질서의 일부입니다. 이해하기 어렵지 않습니다, 그렇지 않습니까? 하나님의 계획을 따르는 가정은 복된 상황입니다. 젊은이들은 권위 아래에 있는 것을 배우십시오. 그것을 여러분의 높은 우선순위로 삼으십시오. 권위 아래에 있는 법을 빨리 배울수록 인생의 책임을 감당할 준비가 더 잘 됩니다.

저는 결혼 생활을 바라보며 자녀를 가르치고 경건한 가정을 이루려는 포부를 가졌던 것을 기억합니다. 저는 “경건한 가정(Godly Home)” 연재를 듣고 준비가 된 줄 알았습니다. 그러나 제 차례와 책임이 되었을 때, 갑자기 제 마음이 시들고 싶었습니다. 책임감은 그것에 대해 꿈꿀 때와 같은 느낌이 아닙니다. 당신이 무언가를 해야 합니다! 당신이 책임입니다. 당신이 그것을 이루어야 합니다. 그리고 덧붙여 말하면 단지 이루는 것뿐만 아니라 그리스도인답게 이루어야 합니다. 하나님의 영의 기름부음이 여러분의 가정 위에 임할 수 있도록 하여야 합니다. 권위 아래에 있는 법을 더 잘 배울수록 그 책임을 더 잘 감당할 준비가 될 것입니다. 우리가 하나님을 더 필요로 함을 깨달을수록 더 복을 받습니다. 자녀들과 젊은이로서 권위 아래에 있음을 배우는 것을 높은 우선순위로 삼으십시오. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Proverbs 3:1-2).

우리가 이 머리의 질서를 지키면 하나님은 그의 복을 더하실 것입니다. 권위 아래에 있는 법을 더 많이 배울수록 가정을 세울 때 더 복을 받을 것입니다. 하나님의 계획은 복을 가지고 있습니다.

7) 경건한 결혼생활

에베소서 5:21,22,24은 “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”라고 말합니다.

무엇보다 먼저 21절을 보십시오. “submitting yourselves one to another.” 경건한 가정에는 함께 어우러짐이 필요합니다. 이 함께 어우러짐은 경외 가운데 있어야 합니다. 우리가 경외 가운데 서로 복종하면 우리는 하나님의 복을 원하기 때문에 하나님께 순종할 것입니다.

에베소서 5:22,24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” 젊은 여성들이여, 기억하십시오: 아버지에게 복종하는 것은 남편에게 복종하는 것과 같습니다. 독신일 때 연습할 수 있습니다. 이것은 여러분의 인격을 세우는 데 도움이 될 것입니다. 반항적이고 거역하는 여인은 하나님의 복을 가져오지 못합니다.

이어 25,28,29절은 이렇게 말합니다. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” 젊은 남성들이여, 남편은 아내를 사랑해야 한다고 말합니다. 그렇다면 하나님이 누가 여러분의 삶에 아내를 사랑하도록 준비시키기 위해 두셨을 것 같습니까? 어머니입니다! 아내를 사랑하는 법을 배우고 싶습니까? 어머니와 잘 지내고 어머니를 사랑하고 돌보는 법을 배우십시오. 장차 가질 아내를 사랑하는 연습을 하려면 어머니를 사랑하십시오.

33절, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

8) 생명의 은혜를 함께 유업으로 받음.

베드로전서 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” 남편으로서 우리는 아내에게 존경을 베풉니다. 그녀는 연약한 그릇이며 자녀를 낳는 자입니다! 그녀는 인생에서 많은 극심한 변화를 겪습니다. 그녀는 먼저 지치고 더 빨리 힘이 소진되는 사람입니다.

그리고 그는 말합니다. “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

젊은 남성들이여, 어머니와 자매들을 이해하는 법을 배우십시오. 결혼 후에 도움이 될 것입니다. ‘아, 그것은 그냥 여자들이 그렇다’라고 결론 내리지 마십시오. 아니요, 여러분은 하나님의 복을 원합니다. 그들을 알고 이해하는 법을 배우십시오.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” 하나님은 우리가 생명의 은혜를 함께 유업으로 받기를 원하십니다. 우리가 생명의 은혜를 따로따로 유업으로 받는다면, 과연 분리되어 그 은혜의 유업을 받을 수 있겠습니까? 저는 그렇지 않다고 생각합니다. 그는 우리가 함께 유업을 받음으로 우리의 기도가 막히지 않게 하자고 말합니다. 그러므로 우리가 따로 유업을 받는다면 우리의 기도가 막히게 되겠습니까? 그렇습니다, 우리의 기도는 막힐 것입니다. 아내에게 연약한 그릇으로서 존경을 드립시다. 이 분야에서 얻을 수 있는 모든 것은 나중에 여러분에게 복만을 가져다줄 것입니다. 그만한 가치가 있습니다. 하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

9) 복되고 안전한 가정

이것은 부분적으로 베드로전서 3:7에서 온 것이지만 시편 144:12에서도 나옵니다. “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” 하나님의 은혜는 연합이 있는 안전한 가정 위에 있습니다. 아버지가 어머니를 이해하고, 아버지가 어머니를 돌보는 곳. 아버지가 섬기며 도와주고 인도하며 긍휼의 마음으로 방향을 제시하는 곳. 남성과 여성에 대한 하나님의 계획—하나님의 계획은 복을 가져옵니다.

10) 그리스도와 교회처럼

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. “Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

나는 진찰실로 다시 들어가며 한숨을 쉬었다. 그녀가 갈 곳을 못 찾을까 봐 두려웠다.

나는 그들에게 계획을 알렸고, 남편은 힘주어 고개를 끄덕였지만, 엘시는 계속 묵묵히 바닥만 바라보고 있었다. “가기 전에 함께 기도해도 될까요?” 내가 물었고, 그들이 동의하자 나는 그들과 함께 기도하며 자유와 예수님의 임재를 두 사람의 삶에 기도했다.

그들은 출발 지침과 가야 할 곳에 대한 방향을 받고 내 사무실을 떠났다. 나는 그날 아침 내내 뿌듯함을 느꼈다. 한 걸음 더 나아가 이 중년 부부의 삶에 실제로 변화를 가져왔다고 생각했기 때문이다.

오후 2시경, 재활 시설에서 전화가 걸려왔다. 시설에는 엘시나 그녀의 남편의 그림자조차 보이지 않았다고 했다. 날씨는 맑고 밝았고 시설도 그리 멀지 않았기에 놀라운 일이었다. 나는 가라앉는 기분으로 부부의 전화번호를 눌렀다.

“그녀는 가지 않겠대요!” 남편이 말했다. “그녀는 미리 말씀드렸다고 하더군요. 줄이려고 노력하겠지만 재활 시설 같은 데는 갈 생각이 없대요. 아마 ‘마음이 바뀌면 알려주겠다’고 말해 달라죠.”

간호사가 재활 시설에 나쁜 소식을 알렸고, 나는 의자에 앉아 멍해졌다. 내가 더 할 수 있는 일이 무엇이었을까? 엘시에게 어떤 다른 말을 했더라면 그녀의 삶에 변화를 가져올 수 있었을까?

약 1년 후, 엘시가 집에서 사망했다는 슬픈 소식을 들었다. 그녀가 재활에 갔고 예수님께 맡겼더라면 상황이 달라졌을 것이라고 확신했다. 그런 일은 일어나지 않았고, 나는 냉소가 내 마음에 스며드는 것을 느꼈다.

냉소주의

우리는 냉소주의의 시대에 살고 있다. 고대 그리스에서 냉소주의자들은 심술궂고 사람들에게 모욕적인(그들은 진실을 말한다고 여겼을 것이다) 말을 즐겨 하는 이상한 부류의 사람들이었다. 그들은 종종 누더기를 걸치고 행동하여 예의 바른 아테네인들 중 대부분이 가까이하고 싶어 하지 않았다.

오늘날 냉소주의는 사람들과 상황에 대해 최악을 믿는 경향을 뜻한다. 냉소적인 사람들은 모든 사람이 오로지 이기심으로만 동기 부여된다고 믿고, 불행한 사건들이 지배할 것이라고 본다.

많은 젊은 의사들은 이상주의적이고 매우 희망에 차 있다. 그들은 최선을 다하면 환자들의 삶에 진정한 긍정적 영향을 미칠 수 있다고 믿는다. 안타깝게도 시간이 흐르고 최선을 다해도 환자들이 변하지 않으면 포기하게 될 수 있다. 이런 의사들은 여전히 시도는 하지만, 더 이상 그들의 노력이 큰 차이를 만들 것이라고 진정으로 기대하지 않는다.

정치에 관여하는 사람들은 처음에는 최선의 의도를 가진 경우가 많다. 그들은 이것이 사회를 더 나은 방향으로 바꾸는 길이라고 본다. 그러나 시간이 흐르고 책임을 지는 얼굴들이 바뀌어도 정책이 크게 변하지 않으면, 그들은 냉소적으로 변하는 경향이 있다.

때로 이러한 냉소는 모든 정치인에 대한 것이기도 하고, 때로는 상대 정당 구성원들에 대한 분노에 국한되기도 한다. 희망은 냉소로 대체된다.

성경 속의 냉소주의

성경에서 냉소적인 사람이 쓴 것처럼 보이는 책이 있다면, 그것은 전도서일 것이다. 우리가 솔로몬으로 이해하는 전도자는 기쁨을 찾기 위해 그가 시도한 모든 것들을 나열한다.

2장 17-23절에서 솔로몬은 일을 헛된 것으로 묘사한다. 그는 다음과 같이 끝맺는다. “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

그는 세상이 폭군들에 의해 지배되며 백성들이 할 수 있는 일이 거의 없다고 보았다. 솔로몬은 정치 권력이 무의미하다고까지 말한다. “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

전도서 6:6에서는 장수를 깎아내리는 듯하다. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

물론 그는 짧은 책을 우리 젊은 시절에 창조주를 기억하라는 지침으로 마무리한다. 약간의 기운이 남아 있을 때 하나님을 향하는 사람들에게는 복이 있다. 늙고 냉소적인 솔로몬 같은 때가 아니라 젊을 때다.

나중에는 하나님께서 그분의 백성을 포기하신 것처럼 보이기도 한다. 하나님은 여전히 선지자들을 보내셨지만, 백성이 응답을 거부할 것을 의심치 않으셨다. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

신약에서도 바울은 디모데에게 사람들이 건전한 교훈을 더 이상 듣지 않을 때가 올 것이라고 말했다. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

이 구절들을 골라 읽으면 미래와 특히 사람들이 변화하려는 의지에 대해 몹시 암울한 관점을 갖게 될 수 있다. 주변 사람들에게 투자할 필요가 별로 없다고 느껴질 것이다. 그들은 비애로 가득 차 있고 다람쥐가 미적분학을 마스터할 가능성만큼이나 변할 가능성이 적다.

냉소의 반대

냉소의 반대는 희망이다. 그것은 미래가 더 나아질 수 있다는 믿음이다.

사도 바울이 로마서에서 환난에 대해 말한 것은 흥미롭다. “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

우리가 겪는 시련을 자랑하는 경지에 이르지는 못했을지라도, 분명히 그 시련들이 그가 언급한 다른 것들을 우리에게 가져다주어야 한다. 우리는 시련을 겪으면서 인내와 경험으로 성장하고, 더 나아가 내일에 대한 희망을 갖게 된다. 왜냐하면 우리는 위대한 하나님을 섬기기 때문이다.

누가복음 15장의 탕자의 이야기에서 대조는 희망에 대해 많은 것을 가르쳐 준다. 아버지와 큰아들은 태도에서 극명히 달랐다.

아버지는 희망을 포기하지 않았다—그는 아들이 자신을 실망시키고 올바른 길에서 멀리 떠났음을 알았지만, 그래도 탕자가 자책하고 돌아오기를 바라셨다.

반면 큰아들은 동생에 대해 희망이 없었을 뿐 아니라 그에게 화가 나 있었다. 탕자는 돈을 낭비했고 죄 가운데 살았으며, 이제 돈이 다 떨어졌기 때문에 집으로 돌아온 것이다.

분명히 동생을 신뢰할 이유는 없었다. 그러나 바로 그것이 우리 하늘 아버지께서 우리에게 하시는 일이다.

정확한 곳에서 희망을 찾아라

문제의 일부는 우리가 잘못된 곳에서 희망을 찾는다는 것이다. 수년 전 어느 대통령 후보가 “희망과 변화”라는 슬로건으로 출마했고, 당선되었음에도 불구하고 대부분의 사람들은 삶이 크게 나아졌다고 느끼지 못했을 것이다.

이 세상이 추구하는 것들—정치적 권력과 부—을 좇는 것은 공허함을 가져올 것이 확실하다. 이것은 사탄의 패턴이다—그는 항상 과대 약속하고 과소 제공한다.

그가 예수를 시험할 때 한 일이 바로 이것이었다. “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). 사탄이 제안한 모든 것들은 예수께서 결국 십자가 길을 통해 얻으신 영광과는 비교할 수 없었다.

마찬가지로 사탄은 그리스도인들이 가치 있는 것들, 곧 희망을 주는 것들을 찾는 데서 벗어나게 만들고 싶어 한다. 사탄은 그리스도인들에게 정치가 세상을 더 나은 곳으로 변화시킬 뿐 아니라, 세상을 바꾸는 더 쉬운 방법이라고 말한다.

성경은 우리가 하나님과의 관계를 키우고 형제자매들이 그 관계를 그들 삶에서 세우도록 돕는 일을 통해 희망을 쌓는다고 분명히 말한다. 우리가 희망을 가질 수 있는 이유는 사람들이 너무나 훌륭해서가 아니다—그들이 그렇지 않다는 것을 알기 위해 오래 살 필요도 없다. 우리가 희망을 갖는 이유는 우리가 섬기는 하나님이 위대하고 신실하시며 최악의 시련 속에서도 우리와 함께 걸어가기 때문이다.

우리는 자격 없는 희망을 가지고 있음을 기억하라

예수님의 용서에 관한 메시지는 우리 삶에서 다른 사람들을 용서해야 할 주된 이유 가운데 하나가 우리가 크고 불합당한 용서를 받았기 때문임을 분명히 한다. 희망도 마찬가지다.

우리 각자는 희망이 없었고 희망을 받을 이유가 없었지만 어둠 속에서 한 줄기 빛을 받았다. 우리가 주변 사람들에게 좋은 일을 기대하는 데 어려움을 겪는 부분적인 이유는 우리가 은혜를 만나기 전 얼마나 절망적이었는지를 기억하지 못하기 때문이다.

예수께서 우리의 절망적인 존재에 희망을 가져다주셨다면, 분명히 그분은 우리 주변 사람들의 마음과 삶에서도 놀라운 일을 하실 수 있다. 우리가 포기해야 할 유일한 사람들은 구세주께서도 포기하신 사람들뿐이다.

작은 노력도 변화를 만든다

나는 의학을 공부하려 하고 외국에 가서 그곳의 사람들을 섬기겠다는 계획을 가진 젊은이와 이야기한 기억이 있다. 우리가 이야기하는 동안 한 나이 든 남자가 끼어들어 개발도상국에서 변화에 대한 희망을 거의 보지 못한다고 말했다.

그 나라 사람들은 더 나아지려는 관심이 없었고, 기생충 같은 것을 막기 위해 최소한의 노력조차 하지 않았다고 했다. 그런 환경에서는 의사와 간호사가 변화를 만들 수 없다고.

나는 그 젊은이의 마음이 가라앉는 것을 느꼈다. 그 노인은 경험이 있었고 희망을 포기했으며, 슬픈 것은 그는 여전히 섬기고자 하는 사람의 희망마저 빼앗고 있었다는 것이다.

내가 수련받을 때 어떤 외과의가 가정의들은 실질적으로 아무 것도 하지 않는다고 말한 적이 있다. 그들은 환자를 다음 진료일까지 겨우 살려두는 반면, 외과의는 사람들을 정말로 ‘고친다’—문제가 되는 신체 부위를 제거해 버린다고 했다.

그러나 결국 작은 노력들이 변화를 만든다. 나는 뇌 수술을 하지 않지만, 다른 사람의 삶에 변화를 줄 수 있다—아마도 조금의 시간을 내어 들어주고 기도함으로써. 이는 우리 모두에게 해당된다.

그보다 더 중요한 것은, 이런 노력을 하는 것이 우리 자신의 삶을 더 나아지게 한다는 사실을 우리가 깨닫게 된다는 것이다. 예수님은 양들에게 그들이 “내 형제들 중에 지극히 작은 자 하나에게 한 것이 곧 내게 한 것이니라”라고 섬겼다고 말씀하셨다.

설령 누구의 삶도 나아지지 않더라도, 우리 구세주께서는 우리의 소망을 아시고 우리의 노력을 느끼시며 언젠가 보상해 주실 것이다.

기억할 몇 가지

우리는 실패에 직면하면 두 방향 중 하나로 움직이는 경향이 있다. 낙관주의자들은 이 사건이 고립된 일화이며 미래는 여전히 밝다고 믿는 반면, 비관주의자들은 실패가 영구적이고 개인적이며 만연하다고 본다.

비관주의자들은 자신의 실패가 내재적 성격 결함 때문이라고 믿고, 이러한 것들이 그들의 모든 삶에 영향을 미치며 바뀔 가능성이 거의 없다고 생각한다. 의인이 넘어졌다가 다시 일어나는 것과 달리, 이 사람들은 넘어지면 그 자리에 눕고 처음부터 패배한 채로 남는다.

다른 사람을 대할 때 우리는 우리 자신에게 베풀어야 할 것과 같은 은혜를 그들에게 베풀어야 한다. 그들 또한 자라나고 있고, 오늘 실패를 겪었다면 내일은 더 잘할 것이다. 어쩌면 다시 실패할 수도 있지만, 적어도 그들은 ‘더 나은 실패’를 할 것이다.

결론

우리 세상에는 냉소가 만연해 있다. 많은 이들이 더 나은 미래에 대한 희망을 포기했으며, 이것은 이 세상의 제도들에 희망을 걸어온 이들에게는 이해할 만하다. 정부나 군대나 관료제도에는 진정한 희망이 없다.

노래 가사가 말하듯, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” 예수님은 우리의 어둠 속에 빛을 가져오시며, 다른 이들이 우리를 실망시킬 때에도 우리가 계속 나아갈 수 있도록 하신다.

하나님은 우리를 구속하시는 분이시다. 그분은 메시지가 무시당하고 선지자들이 박해를 받았음에도 불구하고 선지자들을 보내신 분이다. 그분은 우리가 과거에 수없이 실패했음에도 불구하고 여전히 우리를 위해 희망을 품고 계신 분이다.

그분이 우리가 버티는 이유다. 그분이 우리와 형제들을 위해 우리가 희망을 가지는 이유다.

How unbelievable it is that God can take a wretched sinner, void of the fear of the Lord, and turn him into a blood-washed saint and preacher of the gospel! In this story, we see God’s life-changing power at work in our hymn writer’s life.

In the small cemetery of a churchyard in Olney, England, stands a granite tombstone with this inscription, written by Newton himself before his death:

John Newton, once an infidel and libertine, a servant of slaves in Africa, was, by the rich mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy!

This epitaph aptly describes the unusual and colorful life of this man, one of the great evangelical preachers of the eighteenth century. His testimony was, “By the grace of God, I am what I am!”

“Amazing Grace” was a hymn published in 1779, with words written in 1772 by the English poet and Anglican clergyman John Newton (1725–1807). “Amazing Grace” is probably the most beloved hymn of the last two centuries. This hymn is estimated to be performed 10 million times annually. It has appeared on over 11,000 albums and translated into about 60 languages. It was referenced in Harriet Beecher Stowe’s anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom’s Cabin. It had a surge in popularity during two of America’s greatest crises: the Civil War and the Vietnam War.

Ironically, this stirring song, closely associated with the African-American community, was written by a former slave trader, John Newton.

John was born on July 24, 1725, in Wapping, England, to a seafaring father, John Newton, Sr., and a devout Christian mother, Elizabeth Newton. His father loved him but was gone at sea most of the time. On the other hand, his mother was tender and nurturing, teaching him the Word of God. She would instruct him in memorizing the Bible whole chapters at a time and took him to church. Unfortunately, when he was almost seven, his mother died of tuberculosis. His father remarried a short time later and sent him to a boarding school. During his time at the boarding school, he made bad friends. His character disintegrated to the point that he was dismissed from one school and moved to another. By the time he was 11 years old, the boarding schools didn’t want him, so his father took him along to sea. He spent the next six years on the Atlantic Ocean with his father.

When John was 17, his father arranged to send him to Jamaica for a well-paying job overseeing a plantation. On his way, while waiting for the ship’s departure, John received an invitation to the home of some old-time friends, the Catletts. It was in this home that John’s mother had died ten years earlier. As he reacquainted himself with them, he got to know their daughter, Mary. John and Mary’s mothers were best of friends. John had been invited to stay four days, but he stayed two weeks and missed the ship to Jamaica.

At age 18, John was conscripted into the Royal Navy, and his life went from bad to worse. He wanted to return and see Mary, so he deserted the ship but was caught, publicly flogged, and laid in irons. His life on the ship was so profane that even the other ungodly sailors cringed at his curses and blasphemies. He gained the title “The Great Blasphemer” and was such an unwanted man on the ship that he was sent to work on a slave ship.

One of the owners of the slave ship where he now worked, offered John a job once they reached the African coast. However, once on shore, he was tied up and forced to work with little food, clothing, or shelter. He sent several letters back to his father during this time, pleading for help.

A ship called The Greyhound was sailing near the coast, which John had now called home. The captain had been instructed by John’s father to look for his son. The ship, while being almost too far from shore to trade, decided to give trading a try. A friend of John’s rowed out from shore to trade. As he turned to leave, the captain asked him whether he knew anyone named John Newton. He did to the captain’s surprise, and John was brought on board to go home.

On board the ship, Newton picked up a copy of Thomas á Kempis’s Christian classic, The Imitation of Christ. He had never encountered anything like it, and he began to wonder if the Christian claims might be true. That night, on March 10, 1748, a fierce storm nearly swamped the ship. Men, animals, and provisions were swept overboard. The storm awakened Newton, the ship’s rotten timbers broken by the waves and floodwater swirling into his cabin. John prayed for the first time in years.

The Greyhound thrashed about in the North Atlantic storm for over 11 days. With little hope of survival, the sailors mechanically worked the pumps, trying to keep the vessel afloat. On the eleventh day of the storm, John was too exhausted to pump, so he was tied to the helm, where he did his best to hold the ship to its course. From one o’clock until midnight, he was at the helm. He feared he was going to die, and if the Christian faith were true, then he surely would not be forgiven. He reflected on all he had done over the past few years. His life seemed as ruined and wrecked as the battered ship he was trying to steer through the storm. During those long and grueling hours, Newton cried out to God like he never had before, and that was the turning point in his life.

That was a day John Newton remembered ever after. “On that day, the Lord sent from on high and delivered me out of deep waters.” Over 50 years later, John wrote in his diary on March 21, 1805: “Not well able to write; but I endeavor to observe the return of this day with humiliation, prayer, and praise.”

Only God’s amazing grace could take a rude, profane, slave-trading sailor and transform him into a child of God. John never ceased to stand in awe of God’s work in his life. He took an interest in prayer, reading and meditating on the Scriptures, and only speaking words pleasing to God.

On his return home, Mary and her parents recognized the change the Lord had brought in John. The two were married on February 1, 1750.

For the next four years, Newton was captain of his own slave ship. This occupation kept him separated from Mary for months at a time. While they were apart, the two corresponded constantly. In his letters, John repeatedly wrote how their love and marriage increased his thankfulness and gratefulness to the Lord. “... When I indulge myself with a particular thought of you, it usually carries me on farther and brings me upon my knees to bless the Lord for giving me such a treasure and to pray for your peace and welfare”

John endeavored to “Christianize” his slave ship by holding Sunday services for his crew of 30 sin-hardened men. He made three more voyages to bring slaves from Africa to North America. As he planned his fourth trip, he became sick with malaria. God used this sickness to end his involvement in the slave trade.

As John began a new chapter in his life, he felt called to be a minister. For more than 50 years, he preached the gospel and was one of the most influential men of his day.

John Newton often composed a hymn to go with his Sunday evening services. In 1779, 280 of these were collected and combined with 68 hymns by Newton’s friend and parishioner, William Cowper, and published as the Olney Hymns. The most famous of all the Olney Hymns, “Faith’s Review and Expectation”, grew out of David’s exclamation in 1 Chronicles 17:16-17. We know it today as “Amazing Grace”. “Amazing Grace” originally had six stanzas, and the last verse was added about a century later. Most hymnals have four or five of these verses.

As minister in the church, John continued to be more and more troubled by the slave trade that was still going on. In 1788, 34 years after he left the slave trade, He wrote a book entitled Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade and sent it to all the members of parliament. This book brought an awareness to the public of the evils of the slave trade. He quotes this, “Needless to say, the capturing, selling and transporting of black slaves to the plantations in the West Indies and America was a cruel and vicious way of life.” With the help and providence of God, John saw the day, several months before his death, in 1807, when slavery was officially banned from England.

When John was in his sixties, his beloved wife Mary passed away. This was a great trial for John, and he spent the remaining 17 years of his life without her.

After John suffered a stroke and shortly before his death, a spokesman for the church encouraged Newton to consider retiring from preaching because of failing health, eyesight, and memory. John replied, “What, shall the old African blasphemer stop while he can still speak? I will continue to preach. Although my memory’s fading, I remember two things very clearly: I am a great sinner, and Christ is a great Savior.”

The last words of John Newton as he lay on his deathbed were as follows: “I am still in the land of the dying; I shall be in the land of the living soon.”

The tune “Amazing Grace” is an early American folk melody. It was first known as a plantation melody entitled “Loving Lambs”. This tune was first published in 1831 in the book The Virginia Harmony. The majority of hymn books published after this time included this song. In 1910, Edwin O. Excell added the last verse, which eventually replaced the last three original verses of the song. His edition of the song is most common in our hymnals today. Several other Olney hymns by Newton continue to be sung today, including “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds” and “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”.

하나님께서 경외심 없는 비참한 죄인을 취하시어, 그의 피로 씻긴 성도이자 복음을 전하는 설교자로 바꾸실 수 있다는 사실은 얼마나 놀라운가! 이 이야기에서 우리는 찬송가 작곡가의 삶에서 역사하신 하나님의 인생을 변화시키는 능력을 본다.

영국 올니(Olney)에 있는 한 교회 묘지의 작은 묘비에는, 뉴턴 자신이 죽기 전에 쓴 다음과 같은 비문이 새겨져 있다.

John Newton, once an infidel and libertine, a servant of slaves in Africa, was, by the rich mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy!

이 비문은 18세기의 위대한 복음주의 설교자들 중 한 사람인 이 남자의 특별하고 다채로운 삶을 잘 설명해 준다. 그의 간증은 “하나님의 은혜로 내가 지금의 내가 되었다!”였다.

“Amazing Grace”(어메이징 그레이스)는 1779년에 출판된 찬송가로, 1772년에 영국의 시인이자 성공회 사제였던 존 뉴턴(1725–1807)이 가사를 썼다. “Amazing Grace”는 지난 두 세기 동안 아마도 가장 사랑받는 찬송가다. 이 찬송가는 연간 약 1,000만 회 연주되는 것으로 추정된다. 11,000개가 넘는 음반에 수록되었고 약 60개 언어로 번역되었다. 해리엇 비처 스토의 반노예제 소설 Uncle Tom’s Cabin(톰 아저씨의 오두막집)에서도 언급되었다. 미국의 두 차례 큰 위기, 즉 남북전쟁과 베트남 전쟁 때 인기 급상승을 겪었다.

아이러니하게도 아프리카계 미국인 공동체와 밀접하게 연관된 이 감동적인 곡은 전직 노예 무역상이었던 존 뉴턴이 썼다.

존은 1725년 7월 24일 영국 왑핑(Wapping)에서 선원인 아버지 존 뉴턴 시니어와 경건한 기독교 신앙을 가진 어머니 엘리자베스 뉴턴 사이에서 태어났다. 아버지는 그를 사랑했으나 대부분의 시간을 바다에서 보내셨다. 반면 어머니는 다정하고 보살펴 주는 분으로 하나님의 말씀을 가르치셨다. 어머니는 그에게 성경을 한 장씩 통째로 암송하게 했고 교회에도 데려가 주었다. 불행히도 그가 거의 일곱 살이 되었을 때 어머니는 결핵으로 세상을 떠나셨다. 아버지는 얼마 뒤 재혼하고 그를 기숙학교에 보냈다. 기숙학교에 있는 동안 그는 나쁜 친구들을 사귀었다. 성품은 악화되어 한 학교에서 퇴학당하고 다른 학교로 옮겨졌다. 11살이 되었을 때쯤에는 기숙학교들이 더 이상 그를 받아주지 않았고 아버지는 그를 바다로 데리고 가셨다. 그는 이후 6년 동안 아버지와 함께 대서양에서 지냈다.

존이 17세였을 때, 아버지는 그를 자메이카의 플랜테이션을 감독하는 고임금 일자리에 보내기로 주선했다. 출항을 기다리던 중 존은 옛 친구들인 캐틀렛 가족의 집 초대를 받았다. 그 집은 10년 전 그의 어머니가 세상을 떠난 곳이기도 했다. 그들과 다시 만나 사귄 가운데 그는 딸 메리를 알게 되었다. 존과 메리의 어머니들은 가장 친한 친구였다. 존은 원래 사흘 초대를 받았으나 2주를 머물러 자메이카행 배를 놓쳤다.

18세에 존은 영국 해군에 징집되었고 그의 삶은 더욱 악화되었다. 그는 메리를 보러 돌아가고 싶어 배를 도망쳤다가 붙잡혀 공개로 태형을 당하고 쇠사슬에 묶였다. 배 위에서의 그의 생활은 너무나 불경했기에 다른 불경한 선원들조차도 그의 저주와 신성모독을 보고 몸서리를 쳤다. 그는 ‘위대한 신성모독자(The Great Blasphemer)’라는 별명을 얻었고, 배에서는 원치 않는 사람이 되어 노예선에서 일하도록 보내졌다.

그가 일하던 노예선의 주인 중 한 사람은 아프리카 해안에 도착하면 그를 고용하겠다고 제안했다. 그러나 상륙하자마자 그는 묶여 거의 음식과 옷, 피난처도 없이 강제로 일하게 되었다. 이 기간 동안 그는 여러 통의 편지를 아버지에게 보내 도와달라고 애원했다.

The Greyhound(그레이하운드)라는 배가 그가 이제 고향이라 부를 만큼 가까운 연안에서 항해하고 있었다. 선장은 존의 아버지로부터 아들을 찾으라는 지시를 받았다. 배는 무역하기에는 거의 멀리 떨어져 있었지만 거래를 시도하기로 했다. 존의 친구 한 사람이 무역을 위해 해안에서 노를 젓고 나왔다. 그가 떠나려 할 때 선장은 그가 John Newton이라는 사람을 아는지 물었다. 그 친구는 놀랍게도 알고 있었고, 존은 집으로 데려가기 위해 배에 태워졌다.

배 안에서 뉴턴은 토마스 아 켐피스의 기독교 고전 The Imitation of Christ(그리스도를 본받음)을 집어 들었다. 그는 이런 책을 본 적이 없었고, 그리스도인의 주장들이 정말로 사실일지도 모른다고 생각하기 시작했다. 그날 밤, 1748년 3월 10일, 거센 폭풍이 배를 거의 뒤집을 뻔했다. 사람들과 동물들, 식량들이 바다로 쓸려 나갔다. 폭풍은 뉴턴을 깨웠고, 배의 썩은 목재들이 파도에 부서지며 물이 그의 선실로 휘몰아쳤다. 존은 몇 년 만에 처음으로 기도했다.

The Greyhound은 북대서양의 폭풍 속에서 11일 넘게 휘청거렸다. 생존에 대한 희망이 거의 없는 가운데 선원들은 기계적으로 펌프를 돌리며 배를 띄우려 애썼다. 폭풍의 열한째 날, 존은 펌프질을 할 기력이 없어지자 키에 묶여 배가 항로를 유지하도록 최선을 다해 버텼다. 한 시부터 자정까지 그는 키에 매여 있었다. 그는 죽을 것이라 두려워했고, 만약 기독교 신앙이 사실이라면 용서받지 못할 것이라고 생각했다. 지난 몇 년 동안 자신이 해온 모든 일을 되돌아보았다. 그의 삶은 그가 폭풍 속에서 조종하려 애쓰던 난파된 배처럼 폐허가 된 것처럼 보였다. 그 길고 힘든 시간 동안 뉴턴은 이전과는 다르게 하나님께 부르짖었고, 그때가 그의 삶의 전환점이었다.

그날은 존 뉴턴이 평생 잊지 못한 날이었다. “그 날에 주께서 위로부터 보내사 나를 깊은 물에서 건져내셨다.” 50년이 넘은 뒤인 1805년 3월 21일, 존은 일기장에 이렇게 썼다. “글을 잘 쓰기 힘들다; 그러나 나는 이 날의 회고를 겸손과 기도와 찬양으로 지키려 한다.”

오직 하나님의 놀라운 은혜만이 무례하고 불경하며 노예 거래를 하던 선원을 하나님의 자녀로 변화시킬 수 있었다. 존은 자신의 삶에서 행하신 하나님의 일을 경외함으로 늘 바라보았다. 그는 기도와 성경 읽기와 묵상에 관심을 기울였고 하나님이 기뻐하실 말만 하려고 힘썼다.

귀국했을 때 메리와 그녀의 부모는 주께서 존 안에 가져오신 변화를 알아보았다. 두 사람은 1750년 2월 1일 결혼했다.

다음 4년 동안 뉴턴은 자신의 노예선의 선장이었다. 이 직업 때문에 그는 수개월씩 메리와 떨어져 지내야 했다. 떨어져 있는 동안 두 사람은 끊임없이 편지를 주고받았다. 그의 편지들에서 존은 반복해서 그들의 사랑과 결혼이 주께 대한 그의 감사와 은혜를 증가시켰다고 썼다. “… 내가 너를 특별히 생각하게 되면, 그것이 나를 더 멀리 이끌어 무릎 꿇고 나 같은 보물을 주신 주를 찬송하며 네 평안과 복을 위해 기도하게 한다.”

존은 30명의 죄로 굳어진 선원들을 위해 일요일 예배를 드리는 등 자신의 노예선을 “기독교화”하려 노력했다. 그는 아프리카에서 북미로 노예를 데려오는 항해를 세 차례 더 했다. 네 번째 항해를 계획하던 중 말라리아에 걸려 병들었다. 하나님은 이 병을 사용하셔서 그가 노예 무역에 관여하는 일을 끝내게 하셨다.

존은 삶의 새 장을 시작하면서 목사로 부름을 받았다고 느꼈다. 50년이 넘게 그는 복음을 전했고 당대 가장 영향력 있는 인물 가운데 한 사람이 되었다.

존 뉴턴은 종종 일요일 저녁 예배에 맞춰 찬송을 지었다. 1779년 그의 찬송 280곡이 모아졌고, 그의 친구이자 교구민인 윌리엄 커퍼(William Cowper)의 68곡과 함께 Olney Hymns(올니 히임스)로 출판되었다. 올니 히임스 중 가장 유명한 곡인 “Faith’s Review and Expectation”(믿음의 회상과 기대)는 역대상 17:16-17에서 다윗의 외침에서 비롯되었다. 오늘날 우리는 이것을 “Amazing Grace”로 알고 있다. “Amazing Grace”는 원래 6절이었고 마지막 절은 약 한 세기 후에 추가되었다. 대부분의 찬송가는 이 중 4절 또는 5절을 수록하고 있다.

교회 목사로서 존은 계속해서 여전히 행해지던 노예 무역에 대해 점점 더 괴로워했다. 1788년, 그가 노예 무역을 떠난 지 34년이 지난 뒤 그는 Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade(아프리카 노예 무역에 대한 사색)라는 책을 써 의회 의원 전원에게 보냈다. 이 책은 노예 무역의 악행을 대중에게 알리는 계기가 되었다. 그는 이렇게 인용한다. “말할 필요도 없이 흑인 노예들을 잡아 팔아 서인도제도와 미국의 플랜테이션으로 수송하는 것은 잔인하고 악랄한 생활 방식이었다.” 하나님의 도우심과 섭리로 존은 1807년, 그의 죽음 몇 달 전 영국에서 노예 제도가 공식적으로 금지되는 날을 보게 되었다.

존이 육십 대였을 때 그의 사랑하는 아내 메리가 세상을 떠났다. 이것은 존에게 큰 시련이었고 그는 남은 17년을 그녀 없이 보냈다.

존은 뇌졸중을 앓고 죽기 직전에 교회 대변인이 건강, 시력, 기억력 감퇴로 설교를 은퇴할 것을 권유했다. 존은 이렇게 대답했다. “무엇이라고, 옛 아프리카의 신성모독자가 아직 말할 수 있을 때 그만두란 말인가? 나는 계속 설교하리라. 비록 기억이 희미해지고 있지만 나는 두 가지를 매우 확실히 기억한다: 내가 큰 죄인이고 그리스도는 큰 구주이시다.”

존 뉴턴이 병상에서 남긴 마지막 말은 다음과 같았다. “나는 아직 죽어가는 땅에 있으니 곧 생명의 땅에 있으리라.”

“Amazing Grace”의 곡조는 초기 미국 민요 멜로디다. 이 곡조는 처음에 “Loving Lambs”라는 플랜테이션 멜로디로 알려졌다. 이 곡조는 1831년 The Virginia Harmony(버지니아 화음집)이라는 책에 처음으로 실렸다. 이후 출간된 대부분의 찬송가 책에는 이 노래가 포함되었다. 1910년 에드윈 O. 엑셀(Edwin O. Excell)이 마지막 절을 추가했는데, 이 절은 결국 원래의 마지막 세 절을 대체하게 되었다. 그의 판이 오늘날 우리의 찬송가책에서 가장 흔하다. 뉴턴의 다른 여러 올니 찬송들도 오늘날 계속 불리는데, 예를 들면 “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds”(예수 이름 얼마나 달콤한가)와 “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”(당신에 대해 영광스러운 것들이 선포되네)이 있다.
